source.title: Geometry of Optimization and Implicit Regularization in Deep Learning
source.authors: Behnam Neyshabur; Ryota Tomioka; R. Salakhutdinov; N. Srebro

record.tranche_reason: Reports a width sweep testing whether test error rises after training error reaches zero, using the same general question as V2 but not the original study itself.
record.gate_note: The paper also compares Path-SGD with SGD and AdaGrad, but those optimizer results do not directly test V4's adaptive-optimizer claim. It does not test random-label fitting, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, dropout's effect, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The V2 width sweep reproduces earlier work, including Neyshabur et al. (2015c), V2's original source. This survey supplies no independent width experiment. Its Path-SGD experiments report the proposed method's performance and do not establish another claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the width discussion: the authors argue that network size alone does not explain generalization and propose implicit regularization through optimization. Their broader conclusion is that a rescaling-invariant path geometry can improve optimization and generalization, demonstrated as a proof of concept with Path-SGD.
record.recipe_differences: The width experiment uses single-hidden-layer ReLU networks, SGD with momentum, and no explicit regularization; it is presented in a survey chapter summarizing earlier work.

fits_no_version.finding: Path-SGD improves optimization speed and reported generalization relative to SGD and AdaGrad; its updates are invariant to function-preserving weight rescaling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimization geometry can affect convergence and generalization in fully connected ReLU networks.

record.problems: The width results are presented as plots without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The explicit zero-training-error width is stated only for MNIST.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting compared with natural-label generalization.
No independent test beyond the reproduced original width sweep.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
The limited-tuning adaptive-versus-SGD generalization claim and its stated qualifications.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Matched dropout-versus-no-dropout generalization results; using dropout in some experiments does not establish its effect.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The reproduced width results agree with V2, but should not be counted as independent supporting evidence. The study identifies itself as a summary combining previously presented material.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
The reported sweep covers single-hidden-layer ReLU networks on downsampled MNIST and CIFAR-10; it does not test other architectures or datasets.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
The claim about adaptive methods such as Adam versus SGD under limited tuning, broader tuning, weight decay, switching optimizers, and language models.
Large-batch versus small-batch training and recipe adjustments.
Dropout effects across training-set sizes and with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

tranche.reason: The survey combines previously presented material, including V2's original source; it supplies no independent width experiment. Its Path-SGD comparison does not test another listed version.
